## music_album_cover

> Square album-cover artwork — single hero visual identity with artist and album metadata.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1024x1024`, aspect `1:1`
**Demo vars:** `templates/music/_vars_examples/music_album_cover.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A square album-cover artwork for the artist The Aurora Sound, titled "Halcyon Tides", released on the fictional label Driftwood Records. The cover is built around a single, instantly readable visual hook tuned to a indie-folk dream-pop register — one symbolic motif rendered with confident graphic restraint, never a busy collage. The artist's identity is the product; the date and tour copy are not.
[2. Action] The viewer's eye locks immediately onto the central motif, then drifts down to the artist name and album title set as a quiet typographic block. The motif holds the visual energy of the record; the type is the credit line, not the headline. A small label credit sits at a corner like a foundry stamp.
[3. Scene] Studio-flat artwork plate. The cover is its own world — no physical setting beyond what the motif itself implies. The background is a flat field of color drawn from the deep teal, faded coral, paper-white palette, with optional soft grain or paper texture appropriate to the genre. No perspective tricks, no real-room photography, no people other than the symbolic motif.
[4. Composition] Strict 1:1 plate with 6% safe margins on every edge. The hero motif occupies a central ~62% area with generous breathing room around it. Artist name sits in the lower-left or lower-center as a typographic block; album title nests under it at a smaller weight. Label credit is anchored bottom-right as a small mark. No bleed crops; treat the plate as if it must survive both a 12-inch vinyl sleeve and a 56-pixel streaming thumbnail.
[5. Style] Album-art identity register tuned to indie-folk dream-pop — restrained palette anchored in deep teal, faded coral, paper-white, single-motif graphic confidence in the lineage of Hipgnosis, Reid Miles, Vaughan Oliver and Peter Saville reissues. Type is a single editorial sans or display serif used quietly. No drop shadows, no rainbow gradients, no stock-photo cutouts, no AI-clip-art chaos. Treat the surface like a printed sleeve, not a screen mockup.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- artist_name: "The Aurora Sound"
- album_title: "Halcyon Tides"
- label_credit: "Driftwood Records"

NO: real famous band names, real record-label logos, real public-figure musicians, photographic celebrity portraits, busy collage, rainbow gradients, drop shadows, lens flare, watermarks, stock-photo cutouts, parental advisory labels
```

## music_concert_poster

> Vertical tour / concert poster — headliner identity with tour name, dates, and city run.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1088x1920`, aspect `9:16`
**Demo vars:** `templates/music/_vars_examples/music_concert_poster.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A vertical concert poster for The Aurora Sound on the "Halcyon Tides Tour" tour. The poster is a single composed plate where the artist's visual identity is the hero — a confident illustrative motif tied to the tour's mood — and the dates and cities sit as a clean typographic stack underneath. This is a tour announcement, not an album cover; metadata reads quickly at lobby distance.
[2. Action] From across the room the viewer reads the artist name first, then the tour name as the second tier, then the dates and cities as a legible run of small caps. Up close, the motif rewards a longer look with embedded detail. The eye should never bounce between competing focal points.
[3. Scene] Studio-flat poster plate suitable for both print run and digital vertical feeds. The background is a flat field drawn from the late-90s silkscreen indie revival register, with optional silkscreen-grade grain. No real venue interiors, no lit-stage photography, no audience crowds, no real city skylines — the poster is its own world.
[4. Composition] Vertical 9:16 plate, 5% safe margins. Top ~58% carries the hero motif and artist name. A horizontal rule (or implied band) separates that from the tour name set in display weight at ~70% height. Below it, a tight stack lists the dates and the cities, set in small caps with even leading. A small credits footer occupies the bottom 6%. Plenty of negative space.
[5. Style] Concert-poster lineage of Jim Phillips, Hatch Show Print, and the modern silkscreen revival, tuned to a late-90s silkscreen indie revival mood. Two- or three-color palette, hand-drawn confidence in the motif, quiet typographic discipline in the metadata. No gradients, no rainbow glow, no AI plastic gloss. Treat the surface as printed on coated stock.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- artist_name: "The Aurora Sound"
- tour_name: "Halcyon Tides Tour"
- dates_str: "MAY 03 - JUN 14 2026"
- city_str: "Portland . Boise . Reno . Phoenix"

NO: real famous band names, real venue logos, real city-skyline photography, audience crowd photos, parental advisory labels, rainbow gradients, drop shadows, lens flare, watermarks, stock-photo cutouts
```
